key_insight: Physics-informed machine learning can predict cRPA-derived Hubbard parameters for transition-metal oxides with high accuracy while revealing physically interpretable trends behind electron correlation and screening.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster, scalable screening of materials for DFT+U, DFT+DMFT, and related beyond-DFT workflows without relying on expensive cRPA calculations for every candidate.
method: Ensemble ML models trained on electronic, structural, and atomic descriptors
Regression-based brute-force search to derive explicit analytical expressions
Physically motivated features including TM-d bandwidth and TM-d/O-p band-center separation
evidence_signal: The abstract reports low test errors of 0.148 eV for Ueff, 0.062 eV for V, and 0.007 eV for J on transition-metal oxides.
watch_item: The models are trained on cRPA data for TM oxides, so transfer to other chemistries or low-data regimes may require retraining and careful validation.
paper_title: Physics-informed Machine Learning Prediction of Hubbard Interaction Parameters
